reasons: The old node proved only aggregate score-family optimality and explicitly denied canonicality; the replacement preserves that result while proving the full complete-normal canonical gradient and bound.
This construction exposes the finite full-normal vector and the singular conditional projection requested by the directive.
The directive requires an observable decomposition of the aggregate-to-canonical loss.
The full projection requires the covariance of the complete normal vector, distinct from the aggregate operator \(H\).

The information bound must be distinguished from the variance optimum inside the aggregate score family.
The cumulative vector \(N'R\) does not span all period-specific tangent normals.
A finite deterministic basis is needed to turn the exhaustive family of observable restrictions into a computable normal vector without adding a spanning assumption.
The aggregate KKT residual alone cannot certify equality with the full semiparametric bound.
The corrected comparator diagnostic must report the full period-specific projection equation.

The full normal projection is the correction omitted by the aggregate score-family result.
A fixed pairwise gradient is the starting point for the complete tangent-space projection.
The canonical projection coefficient is determined by a conditional cross moment with the ambient target gradient.

comparator-promise-table-replace: The positioning now distinguishes the proved full DDD tangent projection from the OVS constant-weight result and no longer claims an unverified just-identified EIF equivalence.
The prior formula measured only loss relative to the aggregate-family optimum.
Comparator loss must include both constant-to-aggregate and aggregate-to-full projection losses.
A single aggregate residual cannot characterize equality with the full bound.
The efficiency-bound alias must refer to the full tangent-space bound.
Variance estimation must use the complete-normal influence value.
The vector remains valid for the aggregate subspace but must no longer be described as the complete tangent-normal generator.
This residual characterizes equality with the aggregate optimum, not by itself equality with the full bound.
The plug-in residual must be labeled according to the subspace it actually tests.
The old definition incorrectly assigned the efficiency label to the aggregate-family optimum.
The old sieve removed only the aggregate normal \(N'R\) and could leave a nonzero tangent-normal component.
The old estimator attained only the aggregate score-family variance.

verdict.note: Accept the complete period-specific tangent-normal basis, singular projection, canonical gradient, variance decomposition, diagnostics, metadata, and gap repair framework. Reject the proposed crossfit estimator and its estimator/variance labels: averaging estimated residual normals alone has first-order regression bias and does not establish the canonical influence expansion.
